title: Auto Glass Services Installation, Completion and Vehicle Release Standard
content:
Operations standard of Crestline Collision & Glass for the work itself on an **Auto Glass Services** job: documentation, a chip found beyond repair limits, what a replacement includes, the urethane safe drive-away time, the forward camera calibration order and the completion of the job.

## Standard text

> The technician photographs the damage and the result (the tier's photo count). A chip found beyond the repair limits on inspection ends the repair job as not repairable with no charge, and the customer is offered a replacement job. A replacement fits moldings where the tier's moldings setting is true and a rain-sensor gel pad where the tier's gel pad setting is true, and is leak tested where the tier's leak test setting is true. The vehicle is not driven until the tier's safe drive-away hours after the installation time. The safe drive-away time has passed since installation. Where the tier's calibration order setting is true and the technician confirms the camera bracket, a calibration order opens on installation, and where the tier's calibration-before-release setting is true the job completes only once that order is completed or its declination is signed. The calibration order opened on the installation is completed or its declination is signed. The customer may wait at the center where the tier's waiting setting is true.

## Course of a job

- **Start** — the technician starts the job at the appointment; the job is in progress.
- **Installed** — replacement glass is set and bonded in place; the installation date and time are recorded, and the urethane safe drive-away time starts from the installation time.
- **Completed** — the safe drive-away time has passed and post-installation checks are done, and the job is finished and the vehicle handed back. A chip repair or an unbonded side glass replacement goes from in progress straight to completed. Completion issues the workmanship warranty plan named for the tier, from the completion date.
- **Not repairable** — on inspection the chip is beyond repair limits; the repair job ends without charge.

## Conditions for completing a job

Two conditions are judged on the company's records for that glass job before it is recorded as completed:

1. **The safe drive-away time has passed since installation.** The clock starts at the installation time recorded on the job; the job may complete at or after the moment that lies the tier's safe drive-away hours later, counted in elapsed hours, and the moment itself satisfies the condition.
2. **The calibration order opened on the installation is completed or its declination is signed.** Where the tier requires calibration before release, the calibration order of ADAS Sensor Calibrations opened on this glass job's installation must show completed status, or a signed declination, before the job completes.

## Calibration order on installation

| Tier's calibration order setting | Technician confirms the camera bracket at installation | Calibration order |
|---|---|---|
| true | yes | opens on installation, for this glass job and vehicle |
| true | no | not opened by this standard |
| false | — | not opened by this standard |

## Boundary cases on the drive-away clock (hypothetical)

Glass installed at 14:20 on a tier whose safe drive-away time is, for this illustration, 1 hour:

| Moment of completion | Elapsed since installation | Condition 1 |
|---|---|---|
| 15:19 | 59 minutes | not met |
| 15:20 | exactly 1 hour | met |
| 15:45 | 1 hour 25 minutes | met |

On a tier whose safe drive-away time is 0, the condition is met from the installation time itself.

## Chip beyond the repair limits (hypothetical)

A technician starts a chip repair and finds on inspection a crack longer than the tier's crack limit. The repair job ends as not repairable, nothing is charged for it, and the customer is offered a replacement job.
